summary: Alexander Rogers was an Indologist and historian who studied at the East India Company College from approximately 1843 to 1845. He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1845 to 1879.

Alexander Rödel specializes in religious studies and Indology. He earned his Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh, where his supervisors were Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw (attested 2008).
Alexander W. Macdonald worked in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Musée de l'Homme (circa 1958–1978) and as a professor at Paris Nanterre University (circa 1978–1991).

Alexander Wynne studied Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin (~1996–1999) and earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (2000–2003).

Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery and was supervised by Karin Myers (attested 2012–2017), alongside studying under teachers including Sherab Sangpo and Khenpo Sherab Dorje.

Alexander von Humboldt studied at Frankfurt (Oder), TU Bergakademie Freiberg, Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, and the University of Jena. He held a post at the University of Jena from around 1794 to 1797.

Alexander von Rospatt is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of London and completed a PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg. He held posts at Leipzig and the University of California, Berkeley.

Alexander von Staël-Holstein studied under Richard Pischel at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology, he taught at Peking University (1918–1929) and directed the Sino-Indian Institute from circa 1927 to 1937.

Alexandra David-Néel was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Royal Conservatory of Brussels and learned under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (circa 1888–1893) and Kazi Dawa Samdup (1912).
Alexandra van der Geer works in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied under Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Sondaar.

Alexandre Langlois was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy (~1815–1832). He taught classes at Lycée Charlemagne, served as an inspecteur at the Académie de Paris, and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (~1835–1854).

Alexis Sanderson studied at Balliol College, Oxford, and under Lakshman Joo (1972). Active in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, he served at Merton College, Brasenose College, and as Lecturer and Professor at the University of Oxford (~1977–2015).

Alf Hiltebeitel, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied at Haverford College and the University of Chicago. He spent his career at George Washington University, serving as assistant professor (1968), associate professor (1974), and Columbian Professor (1981).
Alf Sommerfelt was a linguist who founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924. He served as professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

Alfons Fürst, a scholar of religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology, completed his Promotion and Habilitation under Norbert Brox at the University of Regensburg. He held positions at the University of Bamberg and the University of Münster.

Alfonsa Ferrari was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1937–1941) under Giuseppe Tucci and Carlo Formichi, later conducting post-graduate research there from approximately 1941 to 1954.

Alfred Bloom studied at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. A scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology, he held faculty posts at the University of Oregon (1961–1970), University of Hawaiʻi (1970–1986), and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1986–1994).

Alfred Chilton Pearson was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at King's College School, Highgate School, and Christ's College, Cambridge, where he was taught by John Peile from approximately 1879 to 1883.

Alfred Cooper Woolner, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Principal of the Oriental College (~1903–1936) and held positions as Registrar, Honorary Librarian, and Vice Chancellor (1928–1936) at the University of the Punjab.

Alfred Cort Haddon studied at King's College London and Christ's College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the Royal College of Science for Ireland (1880–1901) and the University of Cambridge (1879–1880 and 1900–1926).
